parsed.why: Constitutional gender-identity protection, protected facility access, low victimisation, and courts awarding damages to trans inmates show working recourse; only residual institutional lag and a pending asylum-detention case remain.

Official hostility toward trans people, government tolerance of bias crime, exclusion from femicide protection, birth-sex custody with documented sexual assault, and no anti-discrimination remedy; document-mismatch scrutiny reaches visitors.

No criminalisation and anti-discrimination plus hate-speech provisions covering gender identity, with one bias-assault conviction; but serious unaddressed hate speech, societal hostility, unresponsive prosecutor, and no recognition procedure.

Criminalised same-sex conduct, no protections, refused LGBT registration under an absolute monarchy, no relief record, healthcare refusal documented; Pride tolerance and inclusive health policy soften but don't offset the closed, hostile regime.

Constitutional protection, court-ordered police sensitisation and conversion ban operating, but airport stops, railway gender-check groping, degraded custody, and repealed trans-specific sexual-violence safeguards leave real friction without systemic targeting.
